sentences.text: The Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan was established by the Government of Alberta to provide Alberta residents with medical coverage for physician and hospital services.
The Plan provides coverage for all insured services required by federal legislation and has expanded over time to include additional services provided by other health care practitioners.
The AHCIP offers three categories of coverage: Basic Health Services, Extended Health Benefits and Alberta Blue Cross Non-Group Coverage.

Basic Health Services coverage, available to all Albertans, pays for all medically required services provided by physicians and selected allied health services such as oral and dental surgeons, chiropractors, optometrists and podiatrists, with a monthly premium for this coverage.

Extended Health Benefits, to help pay for dental care and eyeglasses, is available at no cost to residents aged 65 and older, their spouses and dependents, as well as to widows and widowers aged 55 to 64 years receiving the Alberta Widows' Pension and their dependents.

Alberta Blue Cross Non-Group Coverage, a supplemental health insurance plan for pharmaceuticals and other selected health services, is provided at no cost to seniors and Widows' Pension recipients and their dependents.
Individual coverage is also offered through the AHCIP to residents under 65, subject to a monthly premium.
